text: Why the federal Government is obligated to bail out state and local governments explained simply. Any person that says the states or cities should declare bankruptcy is WRONG and doesn't understand basic economic policy or the effects of states and cities facing budget crises. When the colonies revolted, each colony had severe debt with some in far greater debt than others. The entity of the Federal Government wrapped the entire debt up and assumed it allowing states to clear it from their books. Why? Because each colony fought a war it did not ask for and therefore the federal government owed its existence to the colonies. This is exactly the same as the situation today. Every state and local government is fighting a war they did not ask to be in. A cascade effect of bankruptcies through cities will hurt everyone. Any city the defaults on debt will face less economic activity and an inability to raise funds for future needs. The federal government must assume all debts accumulated during this war because only the entity of a federal government can manage a budget with a deficit. Just like the revolution, the entity of the Federal Government OWES every state and city for it's existence and must assume their debts in a hope to keep them surviving for the sake of the economic stability of American citizens that live in their borders.
